clue.text: Model, if she jiggled around, would be a sex object?

indicators.note: around says the shaken letters go round the other piece, enclosing it
something jiggled is shaken out of its order, so the letters it applies to get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be shaken up
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so Model stands for the letter T

explanation.surface: A model shaking herself about turns into a mere object of lust in onlookers' eyes.
explanation.walkthrough: Model stands for one letter because of Ford's Model T; the comma hides that the model is wordplay, not the woman jiggling.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is an item that arouses sexual desire beyond its normal function, hence an object of sex.

clue.text: Ena's over being grabbed by one who rogers tiger

indicators.note: something grabbed is held inside the grabber, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to roger is to have sex with, so one who does it is one who mates

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means turned upside down, so the name reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the name taken as written, the apostrophe-s being 'is'

explanation.surface: A woman called Ena is being groped by some randy fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: MATER is coined as 'one who mates'. The definition is a predator's name, and a tiger that has killed people is called a man-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-eater is a big cat that preys on humans, the classic example being a rogue tiger in India.

clue.text: Perhaps a jungle clearing broadcast by Peel

parts.note: to air a programme is to broadcast it
to peel off clothes is to strip

explanation.surface: It reads like a jungle programme broadcast by the DJ John Peel.
explanation.walkthrough: Peel looks like the late Radio 1 disc jockey John Peel, which makes broadcast feel natural; here it is just the verb meaning undress.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a rough landing ground, and one cut out of jungle is an example of such a clearing for planes.

clue.text: Our old Queen possibly seen in live sex show openings

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist

indicators.note: an opening is where something begins, so only the starts of the words are taken

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: Elizabeth I is imagined appearing in the opening numbers of a live sex show.
explanation.walkthrough: Bess was the familiar name of Elizabeth I, 'Good Queen Bess'. Live is a verb here, not the adjective it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Bess is a pet form of Elizabeth, used affectionately for the Tudor monarch Elizabeth I; 'possibly' flags this as one example.

clue.text: Pants and takes the line of least resistance?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwear or short trousers, read as a plural noun

definitions.text: takes the line of least resistance
definitions.meaning: second meaning: in electrics, current that bypasses its circuit by a low-resistance path

explanation.walkthrough: Pants looks like a verb (gasps for breath) paired with takes; the second half is literally what electricity does in a short circuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorts are short trousers or underpants, and a circuit that shorts lets current flow through an unintended low-resistance path.

clue.text: Sexy shag that might get your cucumber really big

definitions.text: that might get your cucumber really big

parts.note: hot is slang for sexually attractive
to bed someone is to have sex with them

explanation.surface: A smutty promise that a good romp will enlarge a man's member.
explanation.walkthrough: The cucumber is a real vegetable: gardeners raise cucumbers in heated, manure-filled beds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotbed is a warmed bed of soil, heated by rotting manure, in which gardeners force plants like cucumbers to grow fast.

clue.text: Made to go topless, like a couple of Henry's mates

definitions.meaning: first meaning: having had the top part removed

definitions.text: like a couple of Henry's mates
definitions.meaning: second meaning: Henry VIII had two of his six wives executed with the axe

explanation.walkthrough: Topless suggests a bare-breasted model; here the 'top' is the head. Anne Boleyn and Catherine Howard were Henry VIII's executed wives.
explanation.definitionFit: To be beheaded is to have the head cut off, which both deprives one of a top and was the fate of two royal wives.

clue.text: Buy a copy of e.g. John Major: the Autobiography? Don't be such a nerd!

definitions.text: Buy a copy of e.g. John Major: the Autobiography?
definitions.meaning: first meaning: to acquire a book that is someone's life story
second meaning: the scornful catchphrase telling a dull person to find some excitement

explanation.walkthrough: John Major, the Conservative prime minister, was mocked as the dullest man in politics, so buying his memoir is itself nerdy.
explanation.definitionFit: A life is a biography, so acquiring one is literal; the idiom is a put-down urging someone to stop being boring.

clue.text: Some tit's big ugly organ

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slang for a woman's breast
second meaning: slang for a large nose

explanation.surface: Some idiot is mocked for an ugly oversized body part.
explanation.walkthrough: Tit reads as a fool or a small bird, and organ invites a ruder guess; both halves are slang for body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooters is vulgar slang for breasts, and a hooter is also British slang for a nose, especially a large one.

clue.text: Deployed by strong-arm types prepared to do it with male or female on spec, possibly

parts.words: prepared to do it with male or female
parts.note: bi is short for bisexual, open to partners of either sex

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of spec might be ordered otherwise

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Muscle men willing to bed anyone, possibly on a speculative basis.
explanation.walkthrough: The long phrase is a coy gloss for bisexual, shortened to its usual two letters; the definition reads like more of the same innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: Strongmen flex these upper-arm muscles, so they are put to use by strong-arm types.

clue.text: One who wipes tart

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a person who cleans by rubbing hard
second meaning: British slang for a promiscuous or slatternly woman

explanation.walkthrough: Tart may look like a pastry or an adjective for sour; here it is the insult.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrubber cleans surfaces by scrubbing, and in British slang a scrubber is a derogatory term for a loose woman.

clue.text: Be very scared of quiet sex with decent people

parts.note: the sound for silence
it is a coy word for sex, as in 'doing it'
a brick is a reliable, good-hearted person

explanation.surface: Someone frightened of discreet sex with respectable folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Calling a good sort 'a brick' is old British slang for a dependable friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To shit bricks is vulgar slang for being terrified, from fear's supposed effect on the bowels.

clue.text: City gutted over backbencher Brown, not King, the scoffer

parts.note: the word with its middle removed, leaving its two ends

indicators.note: a gutted fish has its insides removed, so only the outside letters of the word stay
not tells us to drop the letter that stands for king from the name

parts.note: Nick Brown, a Labour MP who served time on the back benches
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A political sketch: the City in ruins, a Labour backbencher mocking it all.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown makes one think of Gordon, but the backbencher is Nick Brown, former Labour Chief Whip. In a down clue, over places one piece above the next.
explanation.definitionFit: A cynic sneers at people's motives and doubts sincerity, so is a natural scoffer.

clue.text: (& 26ac.) Pissed off , pisspoor Duran Duran — i.e. without any ultimate no.1s

indicators.note: pisspoor means shoddy, a mess, so the letters are scrambled
the named letters must leave the pool before it spells the answer

parts.note: the 1980s band, anagram fodder

indicators.note: number ones are the leading letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal of 80s pop group Duran Duran, minus any number-one hits.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix DURAN DURAN IE, then take out A and U (the no.1s of 'any' and 'ultimate').
explanation.definitionFit: To do a runner is British slang for leaving in a hurry, as is to have pissed off.

clue.text: That leaves Maggie an ageing sex symbol

indicators.note: the word that departs from the surname, so it is struck off the start

parts.note: Margaret Thatcher, the former prime minister
the word taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: Reads like a joke that what remains of Maggie Thatcher is an elderly pin-up.
explanation.walkthrough: That looks like a pronoun starting the sentence; it is the very letters removed from the start of THATCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cher, the American singer and actress, has been a glamour icon for decades and was in her sixties when this was set.

clue.text: Electorate embraces Gordon at first — unpleasant after-effect!

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one piece wraps around the other

parts.note: Hanover was an Electorate of the Holy Roman Empire, ruled by a prince-elector

indicators.note: at first takes just the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the initial of the name

explanation.surface: The voters hug Gordon Brown at first, and then regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: Electorate looks like the voting public; it is the historical German state whose Elector became King George I of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A hangover is the headache and nausea after heavy drinking, and by extension any unwelcome consequence left behind.

clue.text: Bring back Conservative Iain's first snooze alarm

indicators.note: to bring back is to return, so the whole string runs right to left

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the name before it

parts.note: the initial of the name
a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: A plea to bring back Iain Duncan Smith, the Tory leader whose dullness sent people to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: Iain Duncan Smith was a famously lacklustre Conservative leader, so 'snooze' fits him in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic and alarm are synonyms for sudden fear that throws one into confusion.

clue.text: He's no longer equipped to reach the top as a singer

definitions.text: He's no longer equipped to reach the top as a singer

parts.words: He's no longer equipped to reach the top as a singer
parts.note: surface reading: someone past it, lacking the vocal range or kit to succeed in music; setter's reading: a male singer castrated before puberty so his voice keeps its high soprano notes

explanation.walkthrough: 'Equipped' is the joke: he has lost his genitals, and that loss is exactly what lets him reach the top notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrato was a male singer gelded as a boy to preserve a soprano or alto voice, common in baroque opera.

clue.text: Rebekeh possibly doing a U-turn with her pointless rag exposed

indicators.note: doing a U-turn means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: Rebekah Brooks was an editor (ED) of the Sun; 'possibly' marks her as one example

indicators.note: pointless means a compass point, south, is removed

parts.note: a rag is a scornful word for a newspaper, here the Sun, the paper she edited

explanation.surface: A tabloid editor does a U-turn as her pointless paper flaunts topless photos.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid long famous for topless Page 3 photos; ED plus UN, turned round, gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nude means naked and uncovered, so laid bare to view.

clue.text: Such as 'Becks' can handle

parts.note: the can and the nick are both slang for prison
a handle is slang for a person's name

explanation.surface: A footballer's pet name, and whether he can handle it.
explanation.walkthrough: Becks is David Beckham's familiar name.
explanation.definitionFit: A nickname is an informal or familiar name, like Becks for the footballer David Beckham.

clue.text: Member's opening device

definitions.meaning: first meaning: vulgar slang for the penis, often called the male member
second meaning: the round handle turned to open a door

explanation.surface: Reads as a club or parliament member's means of getting in.
explanation.walkthrough: Member suggests a club or Parliament; it is the body part, and knob is also British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A knob is a rounded handle for opening doors, and also British slang for the penis.

clue.text: Underwear, sexy without once being shameless

parts.note: brassieres, women's underwear

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following word's letters are dropped from the one before

parts.note: taken as written
ex means former, what once was

explanation.surface: Lingerie that is provocative without ever quite being brazen.
explanation.walkthrough: Once seems to modify the sexiness; it stands for EX, which is cut from the middle of SEXY.
explanation.definitionFit: Brassy describes someone loud, bold and showy, lacking modesty, so close in sense to brazen and shameless.

clue.text: OBN candidate gets to be repellent penetrating a dog

indicators.note: to penetrate is to go inside, so one piece is pushed into the other

parts.note: a cocker spaniel, a breed of dog
something that sucks is awful, slang for being repellent

explanation.surface: A crude picture of a nominee and a dog, best left undescribed.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBN is Private Eye's mock honour, the Order of the Brown Nose, awarded for grovelling sycophancy; the vulgar answer means an extreme toady.
explanation.definitionFit: A sycophant fit for the Order of the Brown Nose is exactly what the vulgar insult describes: an abject flatterer.

clue.text: In Thatcher I envisage a soul mate for Tony

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, running across their boundaries

parts.note: letters across the end of one word and into the next two

explanation.surface: Someone sees in Margaret Thatcher an ideal partner for Tony Blair.
explanation.walkthrough: Cherie Blair is Tony Blair's wife; the joke is that Thatcher and Blair were often compared.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherie Blair, a barrister, is Tony Blair's wife, so she is his life partner or soul mate.

clue.text: Votes for English over Celts, maybe

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: maybe hints the word is only one arrangement of its letters, so they are mixed

parts.note: the letters of this word, reordered

explanation.surface: A ballot in which the English are chosen ahead of the Scots and Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, over puts E on top of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To elect someone is to choose them by ballot, so elects means casts one's vote for.

clue.text: Grope out of place around Kylie's butt

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the words after it lose their letter order

parts.note: taken as written, letters to be mixed

indicators.note: the butt is the end of something, so only the singer's final letter is kept

parts.note: the final letter of the name

explanation.surface: An inappropriate fondle of Kylie Minogue's famous bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: Out of place reads as a phrase meaning improper; out alone is the signal, and Kylie's butt is just her name's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cop a feel is slang for touching someone sexually and furtively, which is what groping means.

clue.text: Leader from Liverpool Echo: "Not love but lust"

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its front letter, taken from the place name

parts.note: the city's initial

indicators.note: not tells us to leave out the letter for love from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: An editorial in the Liverpool Echo newspaper declaring that lust, not love, rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Leader looks like a newspaper editorial, which suits the Liverpool Echo, a real local paper.
explanation.definitionFit: To lech is to behave lecherously, so used as a verb it means much the same as to lust.

clue.text: (see 14ac.)
Stones want half a smacker for crafty personal transport

parts.note: jet is a black gemstone, and these are the plural

indicators.note: half of a word means only its front portion of letters is used

parts.note: a smacker is a loud kiss, and the word is cut to its first two letters

explanation.surface: The Rolling Stones want a smacker of a kiss, half a cheeky lyric.
explanation.walkthrough: Stones suggests the band; here it is gems.
explanation.definitionFit: A jet ski is a small motorised water craft for one rider, hence 'crafty' personal transport.

clue.text: One kept by the old queen's pussy at one time perhaps

definitions.text: One kept by the old queen's
definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: a pussy is a cat
A means one, a single item

indicators.note: perhaps means the letters are one possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: An elderly gay man's cat, once upon a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A catamite is a boy kept by a man for sex; 'old queen' is slang for an older gay man.
